title: kv-cache-attn-kernel-seqlen-edgecase-debug-scratchpad-6
content:
---
KV cache / attention kernel / sequence-length edge-case debug scratchpad
Owner: Asha Patel (eng-serving-runtime)
Collabs: Diego, Riley
Status: draft
---

Summary:
- Investigating a hard-to-repro edge case where certain sequence lengths (multiples of 512 + 1) cause the attention kernel to select a tiled/optimized path that then mis-aligns the KV cache buffer and triggers assertion/index errors.
- Repro is intermittent in canary traffic but fully deterministic locally with the minimal script below.

Symptoms observed:
- Error seen in production canary: "IndexError: index 1024 out of range for KV cache (expected max 1023)"
- Local reproduce produces: AssertionError: kv_cache.shape[1] == expected_seq_len (expected 1025, got 1024)
- Not an OOM; allocation sizes look correct but read/write offsets into the KV buffer mismatch by one in some kernels.

When it started:
- First spike: 2026-02-18 during rollout of model X-2-large quantized profiles (more aggressive kernel selection).
- Correlated with new kernel selection heuristic change in PR #398 (switch threshold from >=512 to >512 for tiled kernels).

Repro steps (minimal):
1) checkout the serving runtime branch with debug prints (branch: kv-seq-edge-dbg)
2) setup env: MODEL=x-2-large, DEBUG_KERNEL=1, FORCE_SEQ=512+513 (see script)
3) run: ./scripts/run_debug_infer.sh --model x-2-large --seq_len 1025 --batch 1

run_debug_infer.sh (local):
- python3 debug_infer.py --model $MODEL --seq_len $1 --batch $BATCH

Example python snippet that reproduces the assert:
- from runtime import InferenceSession
- sess = InferenceSession(model_path, kernel_policy="auto", debug=True)
- out = sess.generate(prompt, max_new_tokens=512, seq_len=1025)

Observed logs (trimmed):
[2026-02-20 13:12:07,123] DEBUG kernel_select: chosen_kernel=attn_tiled_v2 (threshold_hit True)
[2026-02-20 13:12:07,124] DEBUG kv_alloc: requested_seq_capacity=1025, allocated_tokens=1024
[2026-02-20 13:12:07,125] ERROR runtime.attention.tiled: IndexError: read index 1024 out of range (max 1023)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "runtime/attention/tiled_kernel.py", line 342, in compute
    v_chunk = kv_cache[:, read_idx:read_idx+chunk_len, :]
IndexError: index 1024 is out of bounds for axis 1 with size 1024

Notes on kernel selection and code areas to inspect:
- kernel_selector.py: policy changed to prefer tiled kernels when seq_len > 512. Previously it was >=512. The off-by-one here could flip the path for seq_len=512/513 boundary cases.
- kv_cache allocation path in kv_buffer.py: uses next_power_of_two or round_up_to_block(seq_len) but may not add +1 for the recently appended token during generate-step.
- continuous batching path: when batching multiple requests, cumulative_seq calculation might use exclusive vs inclusive bounds.

Commands/experiments tried so far:
- Force kernel to naive_attention: set KERNEL_OVERRIDE=naive -> no error, slower but passes. (Good mitigation.)
- Force tiled kernel: KERNEL_OVERRIDE=attn_tiled_v2 -> reproduce consistently for seq_len 1025.
- Add debug prints to kv_alloc to dump (requested_seq_capacity, allocated_tokens, block_size, last_append_index) -> shows allocated_tokens=1024 while requested=1025.
- Change allocation to allocated_tokens = round_up(requested_seq_capacity, block) + 1 -> temporarily fixes tests locally but unsure of perf/fragmentation impact.
- Re-run canary with allocation +1 patch -> no crashes in 10k requests but need more coverage.

Hypotheses:
1) Off-by-one in allocation: allocation uses round_up(seq_len, block) but generate step expects space for the next token (seq_len+1) leading to read past end when tiled kernel reads the just-appended token in a different offset calculation.
2) Kernel read offsets assume inclusive indexing while allocation uses exclusive sizing. Kernel implementations in tiled path index [start_idx : start_idx+chunk] and if chunk calculation uses inclusive end, it will overshoot.
3) Continuous batching cum_seq logic: when coalescing a new request, the batch's effective seq_len calculation uses previous cumulative length but then kernels get per-request offsets computed differently, causing one request's offsets to be miscomputed by one.
4) Race in async KV write: partial write of last token while tile kernel reads ahead - less likely because we see deterministic reproduce in single-threaded local runs.

Short-term mitigations (prod):
- Rollback kernel selection heuristic to previous behavior (>=512) for canary experiments.
- Force-fallback to naive_attention for models with quantization profile X-2-large until fix is in.
- Add a runtime assertion that checks allocated_tokens >= requested_seq_capacity + 1 and fail fast with clearer log.

Proposed long-term fixes and tests:
- Fix allocation: ensure kv buffer size is computed as round_up(seq_len + reserve_for_new_tokens, block_size) where reserve_for_new_tokens = 1 for tiled kernels.
- Align kernel indexing conventions: add unit tests that validate kernel read slices for edge lengths (512, 513, 1024, 1025, 4096, 4097).
- End-to-end regression test: harness that runs generate with a matrix of seq_lens around power-of-two boundaries and asserts no IndexError or assertion failures.
- Add fuzzing for batch coalescing offsets to catch signed/unsigned or inclusive/exclusive off-by-one mismatches.

Action items / TODOs:
- [ ] Write a focused unit test for kv_alloc rounding + reserve (Asha)
- [ ] Add kernel-indexing test vectors for tiled kernel (Diego)
- [ ] Temporary revert of kernel selection heuristic in canary (Riley)
- [ ] Open PR with allocation fix + tests, include perf run to check fragmentation (owner: Asha) -> linked PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/412
- [ ] Add e2e regression job that runs post-merge against sample workloads (owner: eng-ci)

Notes/observations:
- This only repros when quantized kernel path is active (int8 kernels). Float kernels haven't shown the issue yet. Could be quantization changes alignment assumptions.
- Switching to naive_attention increases latency ~2.1x but avoids correctness issues. For canary traffic we can rate-limit to keep latency budgets.

Breadcrumbs (who to ping):
- #eng-serving-runtime (Slack) -> Diego, Riley, Asha
- SRE on-call if we need emergency rollback of canary deploys

Scratch experiments (commands):
- reproduce locally: 
  DEBUG_KERNEL=1 KERNEL_OVERRIDE=attn_tiled_v2 ./scripts/run_debug_infer.sh 1025
- test allocation helper: 
  python -c "from runtime.kv_buffer import round_up; print(round_up(1025, 512))"
  -> observed 1024 (BUG)
- quick patch to kv_alloc (local only):
  allocated = round_up(requested + 1, block)

Edgecases to add to test matrix:
- seq_len in {511, 512, 513, 1023, 1024, 1025, 4095, 4096, 4097}
- mixed-batch: [512, 1025] coalesced
- continuous generate with prefix caching + append token each step (simulate autoregressive)

Last notes / gut check:
- The logs strongly point to an off-by-one between allocation and kernel read offsets. Tiled kernels are less tolerant because they operate on fixed-size tiles and prefetch ranges.
- Fix should be triaged as high priority for Dedicated/private customers running large quantized models (regression risk).

End of scratchpad.
